newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB holds wheat pool prices steady.
newsitem.headline: AWB holds wheat pool prices steady.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it had kept pool prices unchanged for both 1996/97 and 1997/98 wheat.
"The market has been relatively stable during the week and the outlook for wheat prices is unchanged," said Ron Storey, general manager merchandising.
The price for benchmark Australian Standard White (ASW) remains at A$195.00 a tonne for both the number two pool for 1996/97 and for 1997/98 pools.
The number one pool for 1996/97 is closed.
The USDA's August supply and demand report released last week pointed to higher U.S. production as expected, Storey said.
However, this would be more than offset by lower production forecasts by other major exporters, Canada, Argentina and Australia, Storey said.
While the USDA reports showed a substantial world production increase of 10 million tonnes, the higher tonnage would not be sourced from the world's major exporters, Storey said.
The majority of production increases forecast were in China and the former Soviet Union and this would impact little on world trade, he said.
Consequently, the impact on prices would be minimal, he said. The next pool price update will be September 1.
